title.narrative: Output 5.3. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative:
The Egyptian Ministry of Youth and Sports (MoYS) has improved capacity to deliver needs-based employability services to integrate youth in the labour market and take the specific needs of the COVID-19 crisis into account. Moreover, the MoYS has institutionalized the ILO developed Job Search Clubs (JSCs) and has taken up a lead role in disseminating the JSCs further and making them more digital (through an app for job search skills) and inclusive. In 2020-21, the MoYS has integrated refugees into the program which makes the interventions more inclusive and ensures more disadvantaged people access labour market services.
The Federation of Egyptian Industries has also gained implementation experience in running apprenticeship schemes that are more inclusive of migrants and refugees. In June 2021, based on ILO guidance, the Federation managed to obtain a special exemption from the Ministry of Manpower to provide work permits to refugees and migrants enrolling in the program.
Additionally, the Alexandria Businessman Association has innovated their service offer and included a digital skills profiling app (SkillMap) to help migrants, refugees and Egyptians better identify the skills they possess and hence offer more targeted career guidance and skills services. In May 2021, the ILO supported the adaptation of the JSC methodology to the needs of forcibly displaced people and the COVID-19 crisis. The new JSC methodology is validated and a first round of training of trainers has been conducted. In total, during 2020-21 (with a break from May-November 2020 due to COVID-19), the ILO has capacitated 158 JSC facilitators from the MoYS and other relevant NGOs. In total 18 rounds of JSC were delivered with ILO support and 328 youth concluded the JSC's 10 days activity. Despite several difficulties due to the COVID-19-related economic situation, 68 youth found employment after successful completion of the JSCs. Additionally, based on a MOYS request, an e-learning tool to accommodate the JSC is being developed by the ILO and in cooperation with the MoYS. Moreover, inclusive activities that enhance employability such as apprenticeship schemes together with the private sector, disability friendly courses, for which the ILO provided technical support, are being piloted. The ILO also supported the selection and introduction of a digital skills profiling app (SkillMap) in collaboration with the Alexandria Business association and selected NGOs. Together with the Dutch football association, a new course for employability and social inclusion is being developed and will be rolled out with NGOs and Ministry of Youth and Sports. The aim of the course is to integrate refugees and migrants and support employability for youth through a sports for development program.

title.narrative: 5.3.2. Number of member States with innovative, flexible and inclusive skills programmes and services targeting women, youth or persons in vulnerable situations
Output 5.2. Increased capacity of member States to strengthen skills and lifelong learning policies, governance models and financing system

description.narrative:
The Interministerial Committee on the future of work endorsed the Future of Work strategy in April 2021, which encompasses an inclusive Lifelong learning strategy.
Between December 2020 till 2021, the strategy was developed by the Ministry of Manpower and reviewed by the relevant development partners. Between January and April 2021, The ILO conducted an assessment of the capacities of career guidance and employment services make them more inclusive and female friendly. The assessment report has been presented with concrete recommendations to Ministry of Manpower. Additionally, the ILO has continued its support to the Business and Disability Network in order to play a role in strategy formulation inclusive skills that includes a focus on PwDs In particular, the ILO supported the launching of the disability inclusion portal that is led by the private sector and which is a key element of the new strategy.
As part of the formulation of the Future of Work strategy, the ILO provided inputs on the concept of Life Long Learning (LLL) as well as the need for skills anticipation and future skills needs. The ILO also provided direct technical inputs to the Ministry of Manpower to ensure the new strategy supports lifelong learning and more inclusive skills policies. The ILO together with GIZ submitted the revised version to the Ministry in May 2021.
Moreover, the ILO has been elected as Co-Chair for the Education DPG which gives it a unique position to shape agendas and policies on skills and lifelong learning.
